author: WP07
summary: Explains the Effect base (stock versus compiled mode, collections, pass selection, cloning), the stock-parameter boundary, EffectParameter storage, the GpuDrawParams packet and the five stock geometry effects with worked uses and their defect history. Partly stale at TARGET: BasicEffect now exposes XNA's 21-parameter graph, compiled effects have nine opt-in families, parameters of compiled effects are type-checked, Fresnel is per vertex, Software lights and honours PreferPerPixelLighting, and the draw packet is far larger. The site's Effects System page had the surface and property tables; the object model, parameter semantics, exact formulas and verification history went into two new deep dives.

concepts.text: XNA ships five built-in geometry effects (BasicEffect, AlphaTestEffect, DualTextureEffect, EnvironmentMapEffect, SkinnedEffect) plus the internal SpriteEffect; CNA implements all six natively and adds the always-compiled CNAEXT PbrEffect, SkinnedPbrEffect, ShaderEffect and ColorMatrixEffect.

Stock-effect pixel results come from a specific comparison campaign on specific renderers; a byte-identical fixture result on one renderer pair does not generalise to untested effect combinations or renderer families, and closed defects are kept as evidence, not as present limitations.

target.evidence: CNA code comments and plans cited in the stock effects (e.g. BasicEffect.cpp REMED-GFX-010, SkinnedEffect.cpp Task 895)

concepts.text: The stock-effect histories originate in CNA's first EasyGL/Vulkan comparison campaign, which the chapter uses as narrative framing.
concepts.note: Book framing about which campaign produced the audits; the durable lessons are recorded as the defect-pattern and per-effect concepts.

concepts.text: Effect derives from GraphicsResource and deletes copy assignment; Effect(GraphicsDevice&) creates the bare graph of one technique named Default holding one pass named P0 and no parameters.

The byte constructor accepts a bounded, structurally validated XNA/FNA Direct3D 9 Effect Framework binary and rejects empty input, input above 64 MiB, malformed containers and the MonoGame MGFX container, then requires GraphicsCapability::CompiledEffects.

The compiled route is on in every FNA3D build and behind default-OFF options elsewhere; the chapter lists only SDL_GPU, EasyGL and Vulkan, but TARGET has nine opt-in families (EasyGL, OPENGL4, VULKAN, SDL_GPU, WEBGPU, SOFTWARE, DIRECTX9/11/12), 14 of 25 identities.
concepts.note: Corrected from three opt-in families to nine at TARGET (WEBGPU, SOFTWARE, OPENGL4 and DIRECTX9/11/12 added).

concepts.text: The compiled-effect options default to OFF because each pulls MojoShader translation or an interpreter into a renderer that does not otherwise need it; with an option off the renderer reports CompiledEffects false and construction fails explicitly.
Compiled Effect Framework support is not a compiler for .fx or HLSL source, not DXBC or MGFX ingestion and not the ShaderEffect API; each is a separate input and contract.
Effect::Clone() is virtual and returns an owning raw Effect* — a documented CNAEXT deviation from FNA's garbage-collected reference, because C++ has no collector.
Effect::Apply() is CNAEXT: real FNA exposes only EffectPass.Apply(), not a public Effect.Apply().

FillGpuDrawParams(GpuDrawParams&) is the virtual through which every effect hands its state to the active renderer; at TARGET it is a public CNAEXT member and the base implementation is not a no-op — it publishes the compiled-effect runtime pointer (null for non-compiled effects).
concepts.note: Corrected: the chapter calls it protected with a no-op base; TARGET's base sets compiledEffectRuntime and the device collections.

concepts.text: EffectParameter carries a name, semantic, row/column counts, class/type enums, nested element and member collections and a broad family of typed GetValue*/SetValue accessors.
In a compiled effect parameter records are reflected from the binary and their mutable values are synchronised to the renderer runtime only when a pass is applied.
tokens: Nothing is uploaded until a pass is applied

concepts.text: Technique, pass, parameter and annotation collections store elements behind std::unique_ptr, so a pointer obtained earlier (including a captured current technique) survives a later Add() that reallocates the vector.

Collection integer subscripts return a pointer (null when out of range) and name subscripts return null when absent — XNA's null-when-absent behaviour and a source-breaking change since alpha.1, where the integer subscript returned a reference; range-for still yields references.

EffectPass::Apply() throws InvalidOperationException('Applied a pass not in the current technique!') when the pass does not belong to the current technique, including a null current technique — FNA's guard, mapped onto a defined exception where C# would raise NullReferenceException.
tokens: Applied a pass not in the current technique!

concepts.text: Pass membership is checked with a stable 64-bit technique identity token from a process-wide atomic counter, not with the technique's address, because a technique can move when its collection grows.

setCurrentTechniqueProperty throws ObjectDisposedException on a disposed effect, ArgumentNullException for null and InvalidOperationException for another effect's technique; on a compiled effect it also selects the runtime technique index.

Only BasicEffect uses the protected CNAEXT constructor Effect(device, stockTechniqueName) to expose XNA's technique name 'BasicEffect'; the other stock effects keep the bare Default/P0 graph although XNA's compiled stock effects name their techniques after the effect ('SpriteBatch' for SpriteEffect).
Effect::Dispose clears the device's current effect if it is this effect and releases a compiled runtime, so a later draw fails with 'no effect has been applied' rather than touching a dead object.

concepts.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
concepts.text: A compiled effect reflects parameters, techniques, passes, annotations, arrays and structures from its binary; pass application pushes the pass's blend, depth/stencil, rasterizer, sampler, texture and shader state through the device.
tokens: exactly as if it had assigned it

concepts.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
concepts.text: A compiled Clone() copies mutable parameter values and the current-technique choice.

concepts.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
concepts.text: The chapter's claim that BasicEffect adds no parameter records (parameters["DiffuseColor"] returns nullptr) is alpha.1-era: at TARGET BasicEffect builds XNA's 21 parameter records with XNA's names and a test pins the authentic graph.
tokens: in alpha.1 it had no parameters at all
concepts.note: Corrected: 21 records with XNA names at TARGET; none at alpha.1.

concepts.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
concepts.text: AlphaTestEffect, DualTextureEffect, EnvironmentMapEffect and SkinnedEffect build small private tables in CacheEffectParameters(): 6, 5, 12 and 12 records for the derived material, fog, matrix and shader-index values.

concepts.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
concepts.text: The hand-built lists are not a full public description: AlphaTest and DualTexture have no Texture record, and against XNA 4.0 they also lack Texture2, EnvironmentMap and the directional-light records, with some shapes (WorldInverseTranspose 4x4 vs float3x3, Bones) differing from XNA's .fx declarations.

target.evidence: CacheEffectParameters in the four effects; XNA 4.0 IL strings; modules/renderers/directx9/src/shaders/xna/*.fx

concepts.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
concepts.text: SpriteEffect has no parameters, so its CacheEffectParameters() finds no MatrixTransform and OnApply() returns before computing the projection; sprite projection is computed by each renderer's SpriteBatch path, and Parameters["MatrixTransform"] is null where XNA returns the parameter.

target.evidence: SpriteEffect.cpp (CacheEffectParameters, OnApply); XNA 4.0 IL SpriteEffect ctor

concepts.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
concepts.text: The normal render flow is one-way: a stock property writes the effect's field, OnApply() refreshes the parameter records, and at each draw GraphicsDevice calls FillGpuDrawParams(), which reads the fields — not the collection.

concepts.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
concepts.text: Writing a manually found stock parameter is not a portable substitute for the property: derived records (DiffuseColor, WorldViewProj, FogVector, ShaderIndex, light records) are overwritten by the next OnApply() and never read by the draw.

concepts.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
concepts.text: Some properties use their parameter record as storage (FogColor on the fog-capable effects; SpecularColor, SpecularPower, Texture on BasicEffect; SpecularColor, SpecularPower and the bone palette on SkinnedEffect), so a SetValue there does change the draw until the next property assignment.

target.evidence: getters reading *Param_ in BasicEffect.cpp, AlphaTestEffect.cpp, SkinnedEffect.cpp; BasicEffectTests.cpp

concepts.note: Corrected and extended: the chapter names only fog colour; TARGET has further storage-backed properties.

concepts.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
concepts.text: Use the public stock-effect properties for material state and ShaderEffect::SetUniformXxx() for a custom uniform, subject to renderer limits.

concepts.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
concepts.text: BasicEffect's OnApply() reproduces FNA's derived values: WorldViewProj, the fog vector (zero with fog off, {0,0,0,1} when FogStart == FogEnd), alpha-premultiplied colours, eye position, zeroed disabled lights and the ShaderIndex rule; a test checks the populated values.

concepts.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
concepts.text: The five geometry stock effects also load through built-in XNB readers (BasicEffectReader and siblings) that need no compiled-effect capability.
A CNA-constructed EffectParameter stores independent C++ caches — integers, floats, a string and one raw pointer per texture overload — rather than one typed value.

The chapter says parameter metadata never checks that a setter matches the declared class, type or shape; at TARGET that holds only for CNA-constructed records (apart from numeric access to Object-class records), while compiled-effect records enforce XNA's InvalidCastException rules.
concepts.note: Corrected: compiled parameters are type-checked (FX-089/FX-105).

concepts.text: Array getters on CNA-constructed records return at most the stored entries; compiled records return exactly the requested count, zero-filled past storage.
concepts.note: Extended with the compiled-mode behaviour.

concepts.text: A negative array-getter count no longer forms an invalid iterator range: every array getter refuses count <= 0 with ArgumentOutOfRangeException in both storage models.
concepts.note: Corrected: RequirePositiveArrayCount throws for count <= 0.

concepts.text: CNA keeps a separate raw slot per texture overload on CNA-constructed records, so SetValue(Texture*) does not populate GetValueTexture2D(); there is no generic texture getter.
FNA keeps one texture reference that its typed getters cast; CNA's compiled records now do the same (dynamic_cast plus a declared-type check) and refuse a disposed texture or a bound render target.
concepts.note: Extended: compiled mode matches FNA's single reference.

concepts.text: SetValue(string): FNA throws NotImplementedException; CNA-constructed records store any string, and compiled records follow XNA 4.0 (InvalidCastException unless the parameter is a String, value kept per instance and never uploaded).
concepts.note: Corrected: the chapter describes only the lenient CNA mode.

concepts.text: No pointer stored in a parameter retains a texture, and a SetValue on a CNA-constructed record is not a GPU binding instruction.

Standalone parameter tests (EffectParameterTests.cpp) cover round trips and defaults, compiled-mode type checks are exercised in EffectTests.cpp and the compiled-effect conformance gate; lenient-mode metadata mismatch, texture lifetime and stock-effect linkage are not covered by a dedicated test.
concepts.note: Updated coverage statement: 55 standalone tests; compiled checks live in EffectTests.cpp.

concepts.text: Effect::Apply() calls OnApply() and makes the effect current even when CurrentTechnique is null or unrelated — for stock, bare and source effects; a compiled effect refuses a null technique ('A compiled effect cannot be applied with a null CurrentTechnique.').
tokens: A compiled effect cannot be applied with a null CurrentTechnique.
concepts.note: Extended with the compiled-effect refusal.

concepts.text: The familiar per-pass loop is safe because EffectPass::Apply() compares its technique's identity token with the current technique before applying.
The public constructors allow an ownerless EffectPass; applying it returns silently without setting any effect, where FNA only builds passes internally.
Keep application code on the current technique's own passes; null or unrelated techniques and hand-assembled ownerless passes are accepted by the C++ types but are not a configuration API.

Because the device reads a stock effect at each draw (ExtractMatrices plus FillGpuDrawParams), a stock property changed after Apply() reaches the next draw, unlike XNA where state is uploaded at Apply(); compiled effects synchronise at Apply() like XNA (derived from reading, no test).
tokens: captured when the draw is issued

concepts.section: GpuDrawParams: the shared stock-effect draw packet
concepts.text: Every effect's FillGpuDrawParams populates one closed aggregate, GpuDrawParams, defined once in the renderer-contract header and handed with the draw to DrawPrimitivesEx/DrawIndexedPrimitivesEx.

concepts.section: GpuDrawParams: the shared stock-effect draw packet
concepts.text: The packet carries two texture slots plus an environment cube, material colours, three directional lights, the world matrix, alpha test, Fresnel/environment parameters, a 72-bone palette with weights per vertex, fog and the mode flags; at TARGET it also carries shadows, cascades, a punctual light, PBR maps, draw offsets, 16 vertex streams and compiled/custom program pointers.
concepts.note: Corrected: much larger than the chapter's six PBR fields and one custom pointer.

concepts.section: GpuDrawParams: the shared stock-effect draw packet
concepts.text: Adding a new stock-effect input is not a dictionary insertion: the packet, every effect that fills it and every renderer that should honour it must agree.

concepts.section: GpuDrawParams: the shared stock-effect draw packet
concepts.text: specularEnabled is carried in the packet (EnvironmentMapEffect's XNA variant switch) but is read by only some renderers; the Bible's alpha.1-era remark that no renderer reads it is superseded at TARGET (DIRECTX9 and FNA3D read it).

target.evidence: D3D9EffectDraw.cpp and Fna3dDraw.cpp read specularEnabled at 009d40f5 (found by the auxiliary graphics audit package); page corrected

concepts.section: GpuDrawParams: the shared stock-effect draw packet
concepts.text: The claim that preferPerPixelLighting and specularEnabled are ignored by every renderer except D3D9 is historical; preferPerPixelLighting is now read by most 3D renderers.
concepts.note: Superseded by the per-pixel section.

concepts.section: GpuDrawParams: the shared stock-effect draw packet
concepts.text: ShaderEffect fills only customEffectRenderer and customEffectRequested in the packet; the latter lets a renderer without custom programs refuse instead of treating a null program as a stock draw.

BasicEffect implements IEffectMatrices, IEffectFog, IEffectLights and CNAEXT IShadowReceiverEXT; World/View/Projection/VertexColorEnabled are public data members and also get/set accessor pairs, while XNA 4.0 has properties only — the member spelling is a CNA convenience, not XNA parity.

target.evidence: BasicEffect.hpp (World, VertexColorEnabled, accessors); XNA 4.0 IL (BasicEffect properties)

concepts.note: Corrected: the chapter says the public fields match XNA's field-not-property choice; XNA uses properties.

concepts.text: BasicEffect defaults: identity matrices, DiffuseColor one, emissive and ambient zero, Alpha one, SpecularColor one, SpecularPower 16, lighting/per-pixel/fog/texture/vertex colour off, FogStart 0, FogEnd 1, DirectionalLight0 enabled and lights 1-2 disabled, each light diffuse one, specular zero, direction Down.
The early VertexColorEnabled default, DirectionalLight0.Enabled default and light-direction default bugs are fixed; the XNA defaults are pinned by tests.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: constructor sets DirectionalLight0 enabled; tests VertexColorEnabledDefaultsToFalse, DirectionalLight0EnabledDefaultsToTrue and AllThreeDirectionalLightsUseXnaDefaultValues pin the values.

concepts.text: With lighting off the forwarded diffuse is (DiffuseColor + EmissiveColor) x Alpha (FNA SetMaterialColor); with lighting on EmissiveColor x Alpha is added on the lit path — the early no-lighting path dropped emissive entirely.

A disabled directional light is sent with zero diffuse and specular because CNA's DirectionalLight.Enabled setter has no FNA-style side effect; a shared early defect ignored DirectionalLight0.Enabled so a disabled light kept lighting.
Specular is lit-path only; the material SpecularColor multiplies the summed per-light specular once and the eye position is the inverse view translation.
OnApply() computes XNA's ShaderIndex: +1 without fog, +2 vertex colour, +4 texture, and for lighting +24 per-pixel, +16 one-light, else +8; DIRECTX9 and FNA3D select real XNA programs from it.

Per-renderer BasicEffect defects found by the audit — the untextured VertexColorEnabled toggle ignored by EasyGL and Vulkan and DiffuseColor dropped in the textured + vertex-colour case on EasyGL — are fixed; the current packet forwards vertexColorEnabled and the premultiplied diffuse for every combination.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: FillGpuDrawParams forwards vertexColorEnabled and diffuseColor unconditionally; the renderer-side pixel fixtures that closed the defects are CNA's own records (not re-run).

concepts.text: Ambient, emissive and specular forwarding and GPU specular highlights were corrected after the audit; the composed BasicEffect fixture then matched byte for byte on EasyGL and Vulkan at the measured revisions, a result that does not generalise to other combinations or families.
concepts.note: Dated campaign result on two renderers; the current formulas are documented as current facts and the generalisation caveat is on the defect-pattern section.

concepts.text: BasicEffect is the effect a first 3D program reaches for; World may be assigned as a field while Texture/TextureEnabled use get/set accessors.

EnableDefaultLighting() unconditionally overwrites all three lights' diffuse, direction, specular and enabled flag and sets LightingEnabled and XNA's ambient colour, so customise lights after calling it — XNA's own behaviour faithfully ported.
XNA's default-lighting constants: ambient (0.05333332, 0.09882354, 0.1819608) and key light direction (-0.5265408, -0.5735765, -0.6275069); tests check the exact constants of all three lights.
setTextureProperty takes a non-owning Texture2D*; the CNAEXT SetOwnedTexture(std::shared_ptr<Texture2D>) keeps a texture alive through the effect.

AlphaTestEffect implements IEffectMatrices and IEffectFog only (no lighting); AlphaFunction defaults to CompareFunction::Greater and ReferenceAlpha is an unclamped int defaulting to 0, with VertexColorEnabled, DiffuseColor, Alpha and Texture.

The comparison is encoded in one alphaTest vector: reference/255 with a half-step (0.5/255) offset for ordering comparisons, |a - ref| < 0.5/255 for Equal/NotEqual, reference ignored for Always/Never.
AlphaTestEffect has no TextureEnabled switch: CNA always reports texturing on and renderers supply Direct3D 9's opaque-black sample for a null texture instead of selecting an untextured program.
AlphaTestEffect uses FNA-style dirty flags for world/view/projection, fog, material colour, alpha test and shader index.
The audit found no AlphaTestEffect property-default bugs and an eight-value CompareFunction sweep passed on the campaign renderers.
concepts.note: Dated audit outcome on the campaign renderers; the current comparison encoding is documented instead.

concepts.text: Fog was once a total no-op on every Vulkan 3D shader and fog forwarding for AlphaTestEffect was broken on EasyGL; both are fixed — the Vulkan shader set now carries fog in 37 of its 40 shader sources.
tokens: fog that was once a no-op
concepts.note: Positive evidence: grep finds fog handling in 37 of 40 Vulkan GLSL shader sources and the fog vector is forwarded by every fog-capable stock effect.

concepts.text: A cut-out texture (foliage, fence, wire mesh) keeps or discards each pixel whole; AlphaTestEffect performs a test, not blending.

With a vertex-coloured fence the per-vertex colour multiplies only when VertexColorEnabled is true and the product's alpha takes part in the discard; Vulkan once declared no colour attribute for alpha test, fixed with a vertex-coloured shader sibling and discriminating pixel tests.

DualTextureEffect has two independent texture slots (Texture, Texture2), VertexColorEnabled, DiffuseColor/Alpha and fog, no lighting, and reads the second texture from texture-coordinate usage index 1.
The shaders double the first texture's RGB before multiplying by the second (base.rgb *= 2.0), as FNA/XNA do; the factor was missing in all three campaign shaders until fixed.
Saturated 0-or-1 test colours cannot distinguish 'multiplied by one' from 'multiplied by two and clamped' — why the missing doubling went unnoticed.

Texture2's null-texture fallback, DualTextureEffect fog on EasyGL and the vertex-coloured variant were separate fixed defects; at TARGET an unbound texture samples opaque black and vertex colour is honoured.
tokens: An unbound texture samples opaque black
concepts.note: Positive evidence: StockEffectNullTextureTests pins opaque-black null sampling for the stock effects; fog and vertex colour are forwarded in DualTextureEffect::FillGpuDrawParams.

concepts.text: A base texture plus a low-resolution lightmap on a second UV set is the classic pre-baked lighting use; a mid-grey 0.5 lightmap reproduces the base colour exactly because of the doubling.
A lightmap authored for XNA rendered visibly too dark on CNA builds before the doubling fix.

target.evidence: history recorded in CNA shader comments

concepts.text: The vertex type for a lightmapped mesh must carry both texture-coordinate sets and be declared explicitly.

EnvironmentMapEffect implements IEffectMatrices, IEffectLights and IEffectFog with Texture, TextureCube* EnvironmentMap, EnvironmentMapAmount (default 1), EnvironmentMapSpecular (default black), FresnelFactor (default 1), EmissiveColor and three lights.
As in XNA, EnvironmentMapEffect's LightingEnabled is always true and setting it false throws NotSupportedException.
Clone() once omitted FogColor on EnvironmentMap, AlphaTest, DualTexture and Skinned effects; the copy constructors now transfer it and clone tests pin cloned state.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: each stock copy constructor copies the fog colour; StockEffectCloneConstructorTests checks cloned state.

concepts.text: The environment colour is interpolated with the lit base colour, mix(base, env, weight); early code blended additively and over-brightened.

The chapter says CNA evaluates Fresnel per pixel whereas FNA does so per vertex; at TARGET the GL corpus and Vulkan compute the weight per vertex and clamp it to 0..1 like Direct3D 9's COLOR1 register.
concepts.note: Corrected: per-vertex with clamp at TARGET.

concepts.text: Specular is EnvironmentMapSpecular multiplied by the cube map's alpha, not a Phong highlight; the base and specular terms include the combined alpha.
Normals use the inverse transpose of the world matrix, keeping reflections correct under non-uniform scale; EasyGL once used the world matrix.
The 14-property API audit found no property-contract defects and a capstone fixture matched byte for byte on EasyGL and Vulkan, scoped to that fixture.
concepts.note: Dated audit outcome; scoped fixture result not generalised.

concepts.text: A chrome body binds the diffuse texture and the TextureCube, uses EnvironmentMapAmount below 1 for a partly reflective surface and FresnelFactor to brighten toward grazing angles.
The chapter's example calls setLightingEnabledProperty(true) as 'required'; it is legal but unnecessary because lighting is always on, and false throws.
concepts.note: Clarified: the call is a no-op.

concepts.section: Three-light forwarding and a stale plan entry
concepts.text: FillGpuDrawParams forwards the direction and diffuse colour of all three EnvironmentMapEffect lights (zeroed when disabled) and the renderers consume them; early code forwarded only light 0.

concepts.section: Three-light forwarding and a stale plan entry
concepts.text: When lights 1 and 2 are disabled the shader index selects XNA's one-light variant.

concepts.section: Three-light forwarding and a stale plan entry
concepts.text: A planning checkbox (Task 890) stayed open after three-light forwarding was implemented; an EasyGL comment still cites the task number.
concepts.note: Planning-document staleness, not product behaviour; mentioned generically on the page.

concepts.section: Three-light forwarding and a stale plan entry
concepts.text: A three-light scene distinguishes the current forwarding from the old one-light result; a single-light scene cannot.
SkinnedEffect::MaxBones is 72; setWeightsPerVertexProperty accepts 1, 2 or 4 and throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException otherwise.

SetBoneTransforms throws ArgumentNullException for an empty vector and ArgumentException above 72; GetBoneTransforms(count) throws outside 1..72 and restores M44 = 1 as FNA does; the constructor fills 72 identity matrices.
CNA adds a CNAEXT VertexColorEnabled to SkinnedEffect for glTF meshes with COLOR_0; XNA's SkinnedEffect has no such property.
Only the first WeightsPerVertex weight/index pairs are summed, as FNA's Skin(); CNA once summed all four, so assets must declare the real weight count.
Historical SkinnedEffect defects — Clone dropping SpecularColor/SpecularPower, lights 1-2 not forwarded, no GPU specular term, WeightsPerVertex not gating the sum — are fixed.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: the copy constructor copies specular colour/power, FillGpuDrawParams forwards weightsPerVertex and all lights; StockEffectCloneConstructorTests covers clone state.

concepts.text: SkinnedEffect lighting is always on (setting it off throws), with a Blinn-Phong half-vector specular term, fog and three directional lights.
Identity, single-bone and two-bone weighted skinning are pixel-verified on the campaign renderers.
concepts.note: Dated per-renderer result; not re-run and not generalised.

concepts.text: AnimationPlayer::GetSkinTransforms() returns bone matrices already multiplied by each inverse bind pose — the form SetBoneTransforms expects.
Rigs above 72 palette joints must be split into draws with disjoint palettes; set WeightsPerVertex to match the asset, as projects that relied on the old four-weight sum now render differently.
PreferPerPixelLighting defaults to false, XNA's per-vertex Gouraud default.

The chapter lists D3D9, EasyGL, Vulkan, D3D11, D3D12 and WebGPU (BasicEffect only) as honouring the choice and Software as an open limitation; at TARGET a switch reading preferPerPixelLighting exists in DIRECTX9/11/12, EasyGL, OPENGL4, VULKAN, WEBGPU (incl. skinned), SDL_GPU, METAL and SOFTWARE, and FNA3D passes it to FNA's variants.

target.evidence: greps for preferPerPixelLighting in modules/renderers/*; SoftwareRenderer.cpp (ComputeClassicLighting); WebGPURenderer.cpp (skinned vertex-lit)

concepts.note: Corrected: Software now lights; WebGPU skinned per-vertex exists.

concepts.text: A draw that receives a shadow takes the per-pixel path regardless of the setting on VULKAN, WEBGPU, SDL_GPU and EasyGL, because a vertex-evaluated shadow lookup would interpolate into a gradient.

An earlier shared dispatch omitted PreferPerPixelLighting and EnvironmentMapEffect's specular switch, so GPU renderers lit per fragment regardless; renderers added per-vertex variants with FNA's formula in the vertex stage.
AlphaTestEffect and DualTextureEffect have no lighting path, and EnvironmentMapEffect has no PreferPerPixelLighting property.

Secondary findings of the per-pixel fixtures (D3D9 pixel-lit constants uploaded only to the vertex stage, Vulkan pipeline-cache maps leaked at teardown, WebGPU centre values explained by sRGB swapchain encoding, a D3D12 fixture switched to per-pixel) are dated campaign records.
concepts.note: Dated per-renderer fixes recorded by CNA's campaign; not re-verified individually here, and no current defect is implied.

concepts.text: Lit-scene baselines changed when the XNA per-vertex default took effect: low-poly surfaces look more faceted and highlights soften.
Recurring stock-effect failure mode one: a missing shader term (doubled dual-texture RGB, Fresnel weighting, specular).
Failure mode two: a public flag that never reaches GPU state (VertexColorEnabled, WeightsPerVertex, PreferPerPixelLighting).
Failure mode three: a shared dispatch defect affecting several renderers (light enable, fog forwarding, clone-state omissions).
The core interpolation and lighting formulas were not broadly defective; failures were specific omissions, each closed with a discriminating fixture.
